Text:
# DIARRHEA WITH CAMPYLOBACTER

## Primary treatment

Hydration and electrolyte replacement

## Antimicrobial treatment for those with severe disease or risk of severe disease

Fluoroquinolone resistance is increasing worldwide. Macrolide resistance is rare.

## _______________________________________________________________________________

References:
Sanford Guide article: Campylobacter jejuni
DOI: 10.1093/cid/cix669-Shane et al, Clinical Infectious Diseases 2017, 65(12):45-80
Up-to-Date article: Clinical manifestations, diagnosis, and treatment of Campylobacter infection
Therapy:
## Inpatient

Preferred:
Azithromycin 1000 mg PO one-time dose [M]
< OR >
Azithromycin 500 mg PO q24h for 3 days [M]

Alternative:
Ciprofloxacin 500 mg PO q12h for 5 days [R,DI]

## _______________________________________________________________________________

## Outpatient

Preferred:
Azithromycin 1000 mg PO one-time dose [M]
Non-VA order for above
< OR >
Azithromycin 500 mg PO q24h for 3 days [M]
Non-VA order for above

Alternative:
Ciprofloxacin 500 mg PO q12h for 5 days [R,DI]
Non-VA order for above
